children: A Reference Field is how one Document points at another — the raw signal the Edge Extractor turns into every edge in the Content Graph.
Among the field types of Schema v2, the Reference Field is the one that creates structure: it holds the identity of another Document. A reference is either
(many targets). It is declared on a Schema and filled in when editing in LiveView Studio or via a mutation over the HTTP API v1.

References are the only raw material the Content Graph is built from. The Edge Extractor reads each Document's Reference Field values and emits an edge per target; the Edge Projector writes those into the Content Edges Table. So the graph topology is a direct projection of references — change a reference and you change an edge.

The scalar-vs-arrayOf distinction from Schema v2 matters here: an arrayOf reference fans out to multiple edges, which the extractor must split correctly and which expands the Blast Radius of any edit. A reference whose target does not exist becomes a Dangling Reference (and renders as a Phantom Node in the Graph View); a Document with no Reference Field populated at all is an Orphan Node. Plugins that ride the Plugin Behaviour add their own reference-bearing fields — OnixEdit's contributor links, a task's blocks edge — on top of this same primitive. Under a drafts Perspective the extractor re-reads draft Reference Field values rather than reusing the published edges.

References are also what make the Fresh Install Invariant visible: a brand-new Barkpark with the seed Schemas already carries core Reference Field links, so the Content Graph has real edges out of the box — proof the graph derives from content, not from hand-authored topology.
